poster_title: Is Chain-of-Thought Reasoning of LLMs a Mirage? A Data Distribution Lens
authors: Chengshuai Zhao, Zhen Tan, Pingchuan Ma, Dawei Li, Bohan Jiang, Yancheng Wang, Yingzhen Yang, Huan Liu

content: CoT prompting improves LLMs' performance on various tasks.
Empirical successes suggest LLMs engage in deliberate inferential processes.
However, initial findings indicate CoT reasoning may be superficial.
LLMs can produce logically inconsistent conclusions with CoT reasoning.
Models rely on surface-level semantics and token associations rather than logical procedures.
Performance degrades sharply on tasks deviating from familiar templates or commonsense heuristics.
Propose a data distribution lens to study CoT reasoning.
Hypothesize that CoT reasoning reflects inductive biases learned from in-distribution data.
Dissect CoT reasoning via task, length, and format dimensions.
Introduce DataAlchemy for controlled LLM training and probing under distribution shifts.
Design experiments to evaluate CoT reasoning across different tasks, lengths, and formats.
Train LLMs from scratch using DataAlchemy and test reasoning under in-distribution and out-of-distribution conditions.
Analyze the effects of distribution shifts on CoT reasoning performance and consistency.
CoT reasoning is effective on in-distribution or near in-distribution data.
Performance degrades sharply under moderate distribution shifts, revealing reasoning fragility.
Models often generate fluent but logically incorrect reasoning steps on complex tasks.
CoT reasoning is a brittle mirage that vanishes beyond training distributions.
Effectiveness is fundamentally limited by distribution discrepancy between training and test data.
Developing LLMs with genuine and generalizable reasoning capabilities is an ongoing challenge.
